speaker_instructions.Narrator: Warm, grounded storytelling with clear articulation and natural variation. Let meaningful moments breathe. Avoid a sales pitch or exaggerated drama.
speaker_instructions.Roger: A humble, courageous protagonist. Warm, human, expressive conversation with varied pitch and rhythm. Let vulnerability, curiosity, joy, and growing conviction emerge as appropriate to the line. Never a booming announcer or a monotone. In prayers, speak to God personally. Remembrance is woven into ordinary life, not delivered as a sermon. Let fear and trust coexist.
speaker_instructions.Mother: A mature older mother speaking to her adult son. Warm, gently weathered, affectionate, practical and reassuring. Understated, not theatrical.
speaker_instructions.Rita: Gentle and sincere, with quiet conviction and self-respect. Natural, warm conversation.
speaker_instructions.Tim: An ordinary working man. Friendly and direct, with natural warmth. Let frustration or relief follow the meaning of the line.
speaker_instructions.Rick: A successful middle-aged man, kindly and confident. Speak to the craftsman with respect and natural curiosity.
speaker_instructions.Katie: An assured adult woman, elegant, friendly and candid. Natural conversation, never an advertisement.
speaker_instructions.Katie’s father: An experienced older businessman giving patient, practical advice. Conversational, not an announcer.
speaker_instructions.Factory manager: A gruff factory manager, skeptical and dismissive but believable. No shouting or exaggerated villain voice.
speaker_instructions.Coworker: A skeptical coworker teasing another man with dry disbelief. Natural, not cartoonish.
speaker_instructions.Churchgoer: An older, successful man speaking warmly and thoughtfully to someone he respects. Conversational encouragement, never a sermon or grand prophecy.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger worked until the factory windows reflected the lamps inside.

All day, his needle passed through leather.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
At night, he took small repairs home and stitched beside the kitchen table.

Sometimes he fell asleep with the thread still looped around his finger.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He was careful.

He was dependable.

He worked harder when there was less money, and somehow there was always less money.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
One evening, his mother divided a pot of stew among four bowls.

His youngest brother needed a new sole on his school shoe.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
His sister had an examination fee to pay.

Beneath the salt jar lay a notice from the landlord.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger put his wages on the table and watched his mother count them.

She moved a coin from one pile to another, then moved it back.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He wanted to tell her that one day she would stop doing this.

But he could not see how to make next month different from this one.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: Eat before it gets cold.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He lifted his spoon.

He could scarcely swallow.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He did not despise his work.

His mother had taught him that honest work was something to respect.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: But he had begun to confuse the life he knew with the only life he could have.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He called it his fate because he could not bear to keep wanting what seemed impossible.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
The following evening, Roger stopped at a church on his way home.

He stood outside for a moment with his repair bag against his leg.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he went in.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He sat near the back.

For several minutes he could only look at his hands.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
There was dark wax in the creases of his fingers, and a fine white scar across one knuckle.

He had asked so much of those hands.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: At last, he bowed his head.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: God, I’m willing to work. You know I am. But I don’t know what to do differently.
turns.instruction: An exhausted man speaking personally to God. Honest helplessness, clearly voiced, no theatrical sobbing.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
His voice caught.

He waited, then continued.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I want my mother to rest. I want my brother and sister to have a chance. I don’t know how to give them that. Please show me a way. Help me recognize it when it comes.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He had prayed for another shift many times.

This time he was asking to see something he had not seen before.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He stayed until the church began to grow quiet.

Nothing had changed in his pocket when he rose.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Yet he had finally spoken the longing he usually swallowed.

He picked up his bag and walked outside.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Near the steps, a man in a well-cut coat was examining the loose buckle on his shoe.

A car waited by the curb.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The driver had come around to help, but the man waved him back gently.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger recognized the problem.

The small leather loop holding the buckle had begun to split.

He hesitated, then touched the tools inside his bag.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I could secure that for your journey, if you like. It will need a proper repair afterward.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The man looked up, then smiled and sat on the low wall beside the steps.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger knelt and worked a few careful stitches through the sound part of the leather.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Before drawing the thread tight, he silently asked God for care in his hands.

A few minutes later, the buckle held.

turns.speaker: Churchgoer
turns.text: You noticed that quickly. Do you have a shop?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: No. I stitch in the factory. And do repairs when I can.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
The man tested the fastening and asked what he owed Roger for the work.

Roger named a modest price.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The man paid it, then remained beside him while Roger put away his tools.

turns.speaker: Churchgoer
turns.text: Have you thought about taking customers of your own?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: People like me don’t usually get that far.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
The man did not laugh.

That made it easier for Roger to say the rest.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: My family depends on me. I can’t afford to dream and leave them hungry.

turns.speaker: Churchgoer
turns.text: Then keep caring for them. But be careful about what you call impossible.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He looked down at the fastening Roger had repaired.

turns.speaker: Churchgoer
turns.text: A few minutes ago, you saw a way to help me that I couldn’t see. How many other things might be possible that you haven’t learned to see yet?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I wouldn’t know where to begin.

turns.speaker: Churchgoer
turns.text: That is different from there being nowhere to begin. You know the limits of what you’ve tried, Roger. You don’t know the limits of what’s possible. And God has no limits.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger glanced back toward the church door.

The words touched the very place from which his prayer had come.

turns.speaker: Churchgoer
turns.text: What would you dare to build if you stopped assuming the answer was already no?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
The driver opened the car door.

The man thanked Roger again and left.

He had offered no investment, no position, no promise that everything would work.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger remained beside the steps with the payment in his palm.

His circumstances were almost exactly as they had been when he entered the church.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: But a question had entered them.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: That night, after finishing his brother’s shoe, Roger let himself picture a different evening at home.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
His mother putting away the household accounts without a crease between her eyes.

His sister paying her examination fee on time.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: A table with enough for everyone, and something left to offer a guest.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Then he pictured a workshop.

Light over a clean bench.

Good leather.

Customers who came because something he made had improved their lives.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Enough money to pay skilled people well, and enough freedom to choose what he would make next.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
For a moment, the wanting frightened him.

Who was he to imagine such a life?

He almost pushed the picture away.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he remembered the man’s question.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: God, this is what I want. I want to provide generously. I want to make something useful and live fully. Help me bring these desires to You without shame. Guide what I do with them.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He could see the end of his wages.

He could not see the end of God’s abundance.

God’s knowledge did not stop where Roger’s knowledge stopped.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He had been bringing a small picture of the world into every prayer: a few fortunate people, a fixed number of chances, everyone else waiting for what remained.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Yet the One he prayed to was infinite.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger took a scrap of paper.

At the top, he wrote that he wanted a workshop which supported his family by doing work people truly valued.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he began working backward.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
A workshop would need customers.

Customers would need a reason to trust him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Before any of that, there would have to be one person whose problem he could help solve.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He could look for that person before he owned a shop.

He could begin while keeping his factory shifts.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He wrote one thing he could do tomorrow: speak to someone outside the factory, ask what troubled them about their shoes, and listen.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
His mother found him looking at the paper.

He showed her what he had written.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: Can you begin without leaving us hungry?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I think I can begin small.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She sat beside him while he worked out what he could spare.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He put aside a little money, arranged to buy discarded leather with permission, and chose an evening for his first outing.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The next day at work, he made the mistake of sharing his hope before it had grown strong enough to bear much weight.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The first man laughed before Roger had finished speaking.

turns.speaker: Coworker
turns.text: You’re going to make shoes for private customers?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger stood beside his workbench, a length of waxed thread caught around his finger.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Around him, the factory carried on: belts turning, needles striking leather, soles dropping into wooden bins.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I want to try,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Someone at the next bench grinned.

turns.speaker: Coworker
turns.text: Listen to him. He’ll have his name above a shop by Christmas.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger tried to smile with them.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: His manager did not smile.

turns.speaker: Factory manager
turns.text: And who feeds your mother while you’re trying?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: That quietened the room.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The manager glanced toward the door, where men gathered every morning hoping someone would miss a shift.

turns.speaker: Factory manager
turns.text: You have work here, Roger. Don’t throw away what you have for something you’ve imagined.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger looked down at his hands.

A fine white scar crossed one knuckle.

Dark wax had settled into the creases of his fingers.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I understand,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He returned to his stitching.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: For the rest of the afternoon, whenever laughter rose above the machines, he wondered whether it was about him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He kept his head bent so that nobody would see his face.

Anger came first, then shame at how badly he wanted their approval.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Beneath the noise of the machines, he turned inward.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: God, You know how small I feel. Please don’t let their words become the limits I place on You.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He pulled the next stitch through.

His hands were still unsteady.

He asked for help again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
That night, he nearly folded the paper away.

The manager’s question sounded reasonable.

His own hope sounded childish.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Then he remembered the church steps.

Those men knew the factory.

They knew his wages.

They did not know every way his life could unfold.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He took the paper out again.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: God, I’m still afraid. Help me take this one step. Help me see where I can be useful, and speak when I see it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Before his first outing, he sat on the edge of his bed with his coat already on.

His heart beat as though something dangerous waited outside.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He remembered God, picked up his repair bag, and went.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He did not need the whole road to be visible before he could walk to the next street.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He began badly.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He spoke too quickly.

He explained things people had not asked about.

When someone said they were busy, he apologized so many times that they became impatient.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: A shopkeeper asked where his business was.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I work from home.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The man’s expression changed.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: A hotel clerk looked at Roger’s worn shoes and said their guests already had suppliers.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: One woman listened politely, then asked whether he could mend her gardener’s boots.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Yes,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger said.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He took the boots.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: By the end of the first month, he had learned something unexpected.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Being dismissed was unpleasant.

It was not unbearable.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: After one rejection, he stopped around the corner and pressed his palms together to keep them from trembling.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Stay with me in this, God. Help me meet the next person without carrying my hurt into their doorway.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
On another day, someone offered him a chair and a few minutes.

He silently gave thanks before sitting down.

Nothing had been sold.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Still, there was something here to receive: time, attention, a person willing to speak to him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He could be embarrassed at eleven in the morning and still eat lunch at noon.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He could hear no, walk to the next street, and discover that the world had not ended.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Gradually, he stopped beginning with what he wanted to sell.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He began asking questions.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Which shoes did people wear longest?

What wore out first?

When did their feet begin to hurt?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Which pair did they keep buying, and what did they wish someone would change?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Some people hurried away.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Others had been waiting years for someone to ask.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Walking home, Roger began to notice how much he had passed without seeing: a broken fastening someone had learned to tolerate, a shopkeeper who knew a supplier, a craftsman willing to explain a mistake.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
God’s abundance was becoming less abstract to him.

There was knowledge he had not learned, help he had not asked for, usefulness he had not discovered.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He had been living among possibilities while telling himself there were none.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Thank You for helping me notice.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim was leaning against a car outside a café when Roger met him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
One shoe was off.

His socked foot rested on the curb.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Long day?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger asked.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Long enough.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Tim was a chauffeur.

Most days he drove across the city, waited, drove again, then stood beside the car while other people finished their evenings.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: My left foot’s fine,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: It’s the right one. By supper I want to cut the shoe off.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He had already sought advice and been told to return if the trouble persisted.

Different shoes had helped for a little while, then disappointed him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger crouched beside the curb.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: May I look?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim handed him the shoe.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger checked the seams, pressed the lining, and ran his thumb around the inside.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I don’t know whether I can solve it,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: But there are a few things I could try.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: How much?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: For looking? Nothing.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim studied him.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Bring it back before Thursday. I need it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger returned it the following evening.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He had fitted a soft insert beneath the foot.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Two days later, Tim shook his head.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Comfortable standing still. Worse when I’m driving.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger tried a firmer material.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then a thinner one.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he made removable inserts so Tim could compare them during different parts of the day.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Nothing lasted.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Each time Tim returned disappointed, Roger felt a heaviness in his stomach.

At first he worried that Tim would think him useless.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he watched the man ease his foot out of the shoe, and the embarrassment gave way to something more painful: he wanted to help, and he did not know how.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: That night he sat with an unfinished insert before him.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: God, I have reached the end of what I know. You haven’t. Help me understand what this man needs.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He rested his tired hands on the bench.

He stopped trying to invent a brilliant answer for a moment and read Tim’s words again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger began keeping notes on scraps of paper: where the pain appeared, how long Tim had driven, which shoe he wore.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: At night, he laid the scraps beside his tools.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Please help me understand what I’m missing.
turns.instruction: A sincere private prayer. Let the specific meaning guide the emotion: fear, longing, gratitude or trust. Clearly voiced, not whispered or sermon-like.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Once, after another unsuccessful fitting, he offered to stop.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim leaned against the car.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: You remember what I tell you,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Most people just tell me to buy another pair.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: So Roger continued.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He tried shoes with almost no cushioning.

He changed the flexibility of the soles.

He adjusted the room around the toes.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then, one morning, he made a mistake.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Two nearly identical trial pairs stood beneath his bench.

In his hurry, he packed a left shoe from one pair and a right shoe from the other.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim wore them for an entire working day.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: That evening, he arrived at Roger’s door still wearing both shoes.

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: What did you change?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger felt his stomach tighten.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Why?

turns.speaker: Tim
turns.text: Because I’ve just driven six hours, and I’m not desperate to take this one off.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger examined the pair.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The left shoe had the cushioned insert.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The right had the thinner, firmer footbed.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He did not understand everything about it.

But he remembered what Tim had said weeks earlier: the soft cushioning felt worse at the pedals.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He made a second pair with the same arrangement and asked Tim to try it carefully over several days.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The improvement held.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger waited until Tim had left before sitting down.

Relief came over him so suddenly that his eyes filled.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He had been so certain that he was running out of answers.

Yet a possibility had existed that he had never thought to test.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Thank You. I couldn’t see it, but my not seeing it didn’t mean there was nothing there.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He gave thanks for Tim’s patience too.

Without that patience, there would have been no next attempt.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim began calling them his miracle shoes.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger smiled when he heard it, but in his notebook he wrote something more useful:

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The two feet did not need the same thing.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim told his employer, Rick, while opening the car door.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rick had watched him limp at the end of enough evenings to notice the difference.

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: He really helped you?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Tim nodded.

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: Then I’d like to meet him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rick walked every morning.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: One foot was slightly longer than the other, and buying ordinary pairs meant accepting either cramped toes on one side or a loose heel on the other.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: At their first meeting, Roger measured both feet separately.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rick watched him.

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: You seem nervous.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I am.

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: About the shoes?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: About promising more than I can do.

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: Then promise what you can.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger considered that.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I can promise to keep working until we know whether I can make you something better.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rick agreed to pay a materials deposit.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger had rehearsed asking for it all the way to the house.

Rick’s easy acceptance surprised him so much that he briefly forgot the amount.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
On the way out, Roger paused with the deposit in his pocket.

He had spent the journey imagining humiliation.

Instead, he had met willingness.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He thanked God quietly, then wrote down exactly what the money was for.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Receiving help made him want to be more careful with what had been entrusted to him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He spent the next several days visiting shops, examining walking shoes, speaking with suppliers, and studying how different soles bent beneath the ball of the foot.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He could not afford to buy everything he wanted to study.

Some shopkeepers let him look.

One dismissed him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: A repairer across town showed him several worn pairs and explained where they had failed.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When Roger returned to Rick, he brought trial uppers and several combinations of footbeds and soles.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: They tested five arrangements that afternoon.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Two felt promising.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Over the following fortnight, Roger made a finished pair and adjusted it after Rick’s walks.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When Rick finally said,

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: Leave them exactly as they are,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger felt a satisfaction that stayed with him the whole journey home.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Rick paid the balance, then added a substantial bonus.

The total was roughly ten times the original materials deposit.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger stared at the money.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rick mistook his silence.

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: Is something wrong?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Rick
turns.text: Good. My wife would like to see you.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie received him in a room with more shoes than Roger had ever seen outside a shop.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Beside her stood a young woman carrying a notebook.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: This is Rita,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie said.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: She keeps me from arriving at appointments on the wrong day.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rita smiled.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger nearly dropped his measuring tape.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie wanted evening slippers: elegant, fitted properly, and decorated with ornaments she already owned.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She opened a small box.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Inside lay a pair of jeweled pieces shaped like leaves.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger had never held anything so valuable.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie described how she wanted them to catch the light when she walked.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He listened, then set the box down carefully.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I need to tell you something. I haven’t made anything like this before.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie waited.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I understand leather and fitting. I’ll need help with the ornament work.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: Can you find it?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I believe I can.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rita looked up from her notebook.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: It was the first time Roger had heard himself say those words without immediately explaining why he might be wrong.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie took him shopping to show him the shapes she liked.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger paid attention to things he had once barely noticed: the curve of an opening, how a narrow strap changed the look of a foot, the difference between decoration that seemed graceful and decoration that seemed heavy.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He used part of Rick’s payment to buy materials and pay for instruction.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then the trouble began.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The first sample looked clumsy.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: On the second, the decorated leather pulled out of shape.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He tested a mounting method with inexpensive imitation pieces.

It held when the slipper sat on his bench and loosened when someone walked in it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The money disappeared faster than he expected.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Some nights he looked at the ruined pieces and felt foolish for ever having believed he could do this.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The ornaments seemed to belong to a world into which he had wandered by mistake.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He bowed his head over the bench.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: God, I’m frightened. I want to hide from her. Please help me be honest, and help me find the knowledge I don’t have.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He had asked for a solution.

What he found himself able to do first was send an honest message.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He still took factory shifts.

His mother sometimes found him asleep beside the lamp, a scrap of leather in one hand.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: For three days, ashamed of his lack of progress, he avoided sending Katie an update.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: On the fourth, he wrote to her.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
The attachment is not strong enough yet.

I won’t put your ornaments at risk.

I need more time.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Her reply was brief.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Thank you for telling me.

Show me when it is ready.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He folded that note and kept it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The solution began in a jeweler’s cramped workshop.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger had already visited two people who said the job was not worth their time.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The third listened.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger felt the impulse to explain how much he already knew.

He let it go.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Help me listen,
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he asked inwardly.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
The jeweler drew something on a scrap of paper.

Roger leaned closer.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Here was a mind trained by years he had never lived, seeing a possibility he had missed.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He felt gratitude before he knew whether the suggestion would work.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Instead of fastening the ornaments directly through the thin slipper upper, the jeweler suggested mounting them in small settings attached to a separate, reinforced leather panel.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Together, they positioned the decoration on a part of the upper that flexed less.

The jeweler smoothed the metal fittings.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger enclosed the backs beneath a soft lining so that nothing sharp touched the foot.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He practiced with imitation ornaments first.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He bent the samples, pulled at them, and asked his sister to walk around the house in a trial pair while he watched for movement.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Only then did they fit Katie’s pieces.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When Roger brought the slippers to her, she lifted one toward the window.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: Oh, Roger.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: For a moment, he thought he had finished.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then she walked across the room.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Her smile changed.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: They press here.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She touched the front of her foot.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger felt the familiar disappointment rise in him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rita was watching from beside the doorway.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He could have explained how many weeks the decoration had taken.

He could have suggested that evening shoes were never entirely comfortable.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Instead, he knelt.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Show me exactly where.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
His disappointment had not disappeared.

He could feel it while he waited for her answer.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: But he remembered God there too, kneeling beside a customer’s chair, with the work he had hoped was finished beginning again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He asked for the patience to care more about her comfort than about being praised.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He marked the spot.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The next version had more room through the forefoot, a smoother lining, and thin cushioning placed where Katie needed it rather than spread everywhere.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She walked across the room.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then back again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then she kept walking.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: This time, Roger waited for her to speak.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: When can you make another pair?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie wanted heels next.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger sought out a maker who understood balance and heel construction.

He paid for the man’s time and accepted being a beginner again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
There were failed samples.

There were fittings that looked right and felt wrong.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: There was a heel position he changed by a small amount that made a surprisingly large difference.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Throughout it, he prayed.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Sometimes the prayer was hopeful.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Sometimes it was simply,

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Help me stay patient.
turns.instruction: A sincere private prayer. Let the specific meaning guide the emotion: fear, longing, gratitude or trust. Clearly voiced, not whispered or sermon-like.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When Katie settled his fees for the slippers, the heels, and the development work, she added a bonus that left him speechless.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: It was about ten times what Rick had paid him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: More than Roger had earned in the factory in a year.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He counted it at home with his mother beside him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he counted it again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: His mother did not ask what he would buy.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She said,

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: Put aside what belongs to the work.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: They separated the money: household needs, materials, wages owed to the craftsmen who had helped him, savings.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: For the first time, there was still a meaningful amount left.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He looked at the remaining money, then at the piles that would pay other people.

The payment had fed more than one household.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
The jeweler had earned something.

The other maker had earned something.

Katie had received shoes she loved.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger had once imagined prosperity as a small locked room in which a few people kept what everyone else needed.

This felt different.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Something useful had come into existence, and several lives were better because of it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
For him, this was a glimpse of the abundance he had prayed to recognize.

God had not become more generous that month.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger had begun to see more ways to receive, work with, and pass on that generosity.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger sat quietly before it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He had not taken it from anyone.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He had listened, learned, asked for help, and made something another person valued.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Thank you, God,
turns.instruction: A sincere private prayer. Let the specific meaning guide the emotion: fear, longing, gratitude or trust. Clearly voiced, not whispered or sermon-like.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie’s friends began asking about the shoes.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: At first, Roger took one commission at a time.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then there were more appointments than he could manage after his shifts.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie approached her father, who owned several businesses.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
She brought him orders, cost estimates, and samples.

He asked difficult questions.

Some she could answer.

Others she brought back to Roger.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Eventually, they agreed to fund a small company.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Katie would run the commercial side and bring in customers.

Her father would provide capital and advice.

Roger would lead design, fitting, and production.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger’s share would be thirty percent.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Before signing, he paid an independent adviser to explain the agreement.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: It cost him money he disliked spending.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He was glad afterward that he had spent it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The workshop frightened him more than his first private commission.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Now mistakes could waste other people’s wages.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He knew how to work at a production bench.

He had never designed the flow of an entire workshop.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He stood in the empty room the evening before the equipment arrived.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Help me build something good here,
turns.instruction: A sincere private prayer. Let the specific meaning guide the emotion: fear, longing, gratitude or trust. Clearly voiced, not whispered or sermon-like.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he prayed.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Help me recognize what I don’t know.
turns.instruction: A sincere private prayer. Let the specific meaning guide the emotion: fear, longing, gratitude or trust. Clearly voiced, not whispered or sermon-like.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He hired a cutter whose precision he had admired for years, an experienced stitcher, and a production supervisor who had organized work in another factory.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Together, they divided the process into stages: measuring and fitting, patterns, cutting, stitching, assembly, finishing, inspection.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
They labeled each customer’s measurements clearly.

They kept separate patterns for left and right feet when required.

They checked a trial fitting before completing expensive custom work.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger made mistakes.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Once, he moved a workstation because it looked tidier and slowed the whole room down.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The supervisor explained why.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger moved it back.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The employees began offering suggestions more freely after that.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Remembrance began to find a place in the smallest parts of his day.

Before cutting costly leather, he asked for care in his hands.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When a needle snapped and irritation rose, he paused before speaking to the person beside him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When someone caught an error, he thanked God for the correction and thanked the person aloud.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Sometimes he forgot for hours.

He became hurried, proud of a design, frightened by a bill.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he would notice the tightness in himself and return, without ceremony.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Help me with this too.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
A tangled thread.

A difficult apology.

A decision about wages.

He was learning that he did not have to wait for a crisis to turn toward God.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Their first serious business failure arrived in beautiful boxes.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Dozens of them.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Stacked against a wall.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Katie’s friends had loved the early designs, and Roger had assumed that more shoes would mean more sales.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: They had committed too much money to too many styles.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Some sizes hardly moved.

Certain colors received compliments and no orders.

Materials sat unused while wages and rent continued to fall due.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger began arriving before everyone else and leaving after they had gone.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: One evening, his mother found him at the kitchen table studying figures.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: Are we in trouble?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He almost said no.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Instead, he told her what was happening.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
After she went to bed, he remained at the table.

He had prayed before opening the workshop.

He had worked until his eyes hurt.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Why was he sitting here afraid of losing it?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
For a moment, he felt ashamed even of the question.

Then he brought that to God as well.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I thought I was doing the right thing. I don’t understand this. Please help me. Help me see clearly enough to protect the people depending on me.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He wanted certainty that everything would be all right.

None came.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
What returned, slowly, was the recognition that his fear did not know everything.

He remembered the man outside the church.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Not knowing a way was different from there being no way.

These figures described a problem.

They did not describe the limits of God.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: There might be a question he had not asked, an error he had not understood, a person from whom he could learn.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He could not see the whole way forward.

He could ask for help with tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The next morning, he went to Katie’s father.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I know how to make something one person wants,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger said.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: I don’t know how to make enough people buy it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The older man closed the notebook between them.

turns.speaker: Katie’s father
turns.text: Then you have another trade to learn.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He advised them to reduce the range, protect their cash, and stop making speculative stock until they understood demand.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he asked Roger a question.

turns.speaker: Katie’s father
turns.text: When did you last speak to someone who bought from you?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger named a customer he had fitted that week.

turns.speaker: Katie’s father
turns.text: After the sale, I mean.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger had no answer.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Heat rose into his face.

Then, beneath the embarrassment, he felt a small opening.

There was something he could do that he had not been doing.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He silently thanked God for bringing him to a question that humbled him enough to learn.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He began making visits.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He asked before calling.

He wrote down preferences.

He checked whether shoes had remained comfortable after an entire evening, not merely during a fitting.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He learned that one customer loved her slippers but never wore them because the color matched nothing she owned.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Another needed shoes for a particular gala and had ordered elsewhere because she had not known Roger could deliver in time.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: One woman said quietly that she hated having to choose between looking elegant and being able to remain on her feet beside her friends.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger remembered that.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He and Katie arranged small appointments where customers could see samples, bring their dresses, and discuss upcoming events.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: They improved the packaging so the shoes arrived protected, beautifully presented, and accompanied by clear care instructions.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
They asked satisfied customers for introductions.

They made alterations promptly.

They developed a small collection that customers could adapt instead of beginning every design from nothing.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: For the next season, they took deposits before committing to larger material orders.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The unsold boxes gradually disappeared.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: More importantly, fewer new ones accumulated.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger discovered that selling could be another form of attention.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He did not have to become someone else.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He had to keep listening after the shoes left his hands.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Before a visit, he would ask God to help him hear what mattered to the customer.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Afterward, he gave thanks for what she had told him, even when it was criticism.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The world was beginning to feel larger.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: There were more needs than he could serve alone, more designs than he could make in a lifetime, more people with knowledge to share.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He did not need to possess all of it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He could take his place in it, do useful work, and trust that the source of abundance was greater than his grasp.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rita appeared often during those months.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Sometimes she accompanied Katie.

Sometimes she collected an order for another woman she assisted.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger learned that her family had once been wealthy.

A business failure had changed their circumstances, and she had gone to work.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She spoke of it without bitterness.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: One afternoon, while waiting for a small alteration, she helped his mother carry a basket through the workshop door.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Later, his mother said,

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: That young woman has good manners.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger pretended to be occupied.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: His mother noticed.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rita once found him apologizing for the plain room where he received fittings.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: It isn’t much yet,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She looked around at the measured patterns, the clean workbench, and the half-finished shoes.

turns.speaker: Rita
turns.text: People are doing honest work here.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He glanced at her.

turns.speaker: Rita
turns.text: There’s nothing to apologize for,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: she said.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He remembered that sentence long after he forgot what they had discussed afterward.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
That evening, he remembered her kindness while putting away his tools.

He thanked God for it as simply as he might have thanked Him for food.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He was beginning to recognize provision in things he could not deposit in an account: a word that relieved his shame, a person who understood his mother, the courage to be seen before his work was perfect.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The company’s growth took years.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: There were seasons when orders came easily and seasons when Roger worried again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
A supplier failed to deliver.

A promising design sold poorly.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: A large order had to be remade because a material behaved differently in use than it had in the sample.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: But the business learned.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger learned.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
His reputation spread beyond the city.

Customers traveled for fittings.

Invitations arrived from retailers and event organizers.

People began asking what he would make next.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: They paid high prices because the work was distinctive, the fit received unusual care, and Roger’s company had earned a reputation for putting problems right.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He paid his employees reliably.

He promoted people who could do things better than he could.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He gave the workshop time for training and allowed experienced hands to question a design before it became an expensive mistake.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: His days remained disciplined.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He began them in prayer.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He still carried a notebook.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: And when a customer described a problem, he tried to hear it before deciding he already knew the answer.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Success did not remove his need for that inward return.

Sometimes it made the need harder to notice.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
An important customer praised him, and he would carry the words around all afternoon.

A worker questioned him, and he would feel himself stiffen.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When he caught it, he asked God to keep him teachable.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He remembered the first insert that had failed, the jeweler’s drawing, the supervisor who had moved the workstation back.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
His skill was real.

So was the help through which it had grown.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Remembering both allowed him to enjoy what he could do without imagining that everything depended on him.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Success brought attention he had never expected.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Some invitations were innocent.

Others were not.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Once, a married customer suggested that he bring samples to her house late in the evening, when her husband would be away.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger recognized the invitation beneath the words.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: We can arrange a fitting at the showroom,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: he said gently.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Katie will help us choose a convenient time.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When she pressed, he remained courteous and firm.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Afterward, he told no entertaining story about it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Her private embarrassment was not something he wanted to turn into his own importance.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He found that wealth gave him more choices.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He wanted to remain responsible for the choices he made.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Before answering invitations that stirred his vanity, he sometimes needed a moment alone.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: God, help me choose what will leave peace in my home and in theirs.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Then he returned and spoke kindly.

The remembrance belonged there as much as it belonged beside his prayer mat.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: In time, Roger saved enough to purchase a larger share of the company.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He did not empty the business to do it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: With retained personal earnings and a formally arranged loan from clients who had come to trust him, he negotiated to buy another thirty percent.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Advisers reviewed the terms.

The repayments were measured against what he could reasonably afford.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The papers were signed in the same office where he had once struggled to explain his first cost estimates.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Afterward, Katie shook his hand.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then she laughed.

turns.speaker: Katie
turns.text: You still look as though you’ve been called into trouble.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger laughed too.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Some habits took longer to change than others.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He bought a spacious house with a garden his mother could tend if she wished, and rooms where his siblings could return with families of their own.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
There were vehicles now.

There were journeys he could once only have imagined.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He enjoyed them.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He enjoyed buying good materials without first calculating whether it would leave the household short.

He enjoyed paying for his brother’s studies.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He enjoyed giving his mother the freedom to choose something because she liked it.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Abundance had become more than a sum in an account.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: It was room to act.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Room to rest.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Room to help without panic.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He no longer apologized inwardly for enjoying it.

When his mother chose something beautiful for the house, he delighted in her pleasure.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When his brother wrote about his studies, Roger read the letter twice.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He wanted a full life: worthwhile work, a generous home, comfort, beauty, love, and the means to do more good.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He could bring those desires to God openly.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He knew the company had limits.

His time and judgment had limits.

God did not.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He could respect the limits of a particular plan without surrendering his belief in the vastness of what remained possible.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: That recognition made him grateful for what he held and hopeful about what he had yet to discover.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When his mother finally mentioned marriage, she did so while pouring tea.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: There is someone I would like you to consider.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger kept his eyes on his cup.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Who?

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: Rita.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He looked up so quickly that she smiled.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: I would speak to her family,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: she said.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: If you wished. And if she wished.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He asked for a day to think.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: His mother gave him until the following morning.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: When Roger and Rita met to speak seriously, he was more nervous than he had been in several important business meetings.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She made it easier by admitting that she was nervous too.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
Roger felt his shoulders loosen.

He silently thanked God for that small kindness.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He had prayed over large sums of money with more composure than he had managed while waiting for her to arrive.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: They spoke about faith, family, work, and the kind of home they wanted.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger told her that he did not want her to feel she had to hide the years when her family had struggled.

turns.speaker: Rita
turns.text: I don’t,

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: she said.

turns.speaker: Rita
turns.text: We worked. We were honest. God was there too.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He knew then that his mother had understood something he had been too shy to say aloud.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: They married with the willing blessing of both families.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Years later, Roger came home after a long day and found the house quiet.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Rita had left a lamp burning.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: His mother had fallen asleep in her chair with a book resting open in her lap.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: For a moment, he stood in the doorway.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He remembered her hands dividing his wages into small piles.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He remembered the landlord’s notice beneath the salt jar.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He remembered a man in a factory asking who would feed her when he failed.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger lifted the book and marked her place.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She stirred.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: You’re home?

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Yes, Mother.

turns.speaker: Mother
turns.text: Have you eaten?

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He smiled.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: She settled back.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: There was nothing she needed to calculate that night.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Roger stood beside her until her breathing grew steady again.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Gratitude rose through him with the memory of all those small, frightened prayers: beside the factory bench, outside a stranger’s door, over a shoe that would not come right.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He had not known, while living them, how one day would lead to another.

He had only known where to turn.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text: Thank You for caring for us in ways I could not imagine.
turns.instruction: A personal prayer addressed to God. Speak as a real man in this moment, with vulnerability, longing, gratitude or growing trust as the words imply. Expressive and understated, never preaching. No whispering.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
He drew the blanket gently over her knees.

Then he switched off the brighter lamp and left the softer one burning.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: The next morning, he rose before the household.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text:
There was a difficult fitting waiting at the workshop.

A new employee needed guidance.

A customer had written about a fastening that troubled her fingers.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: He washed, knelt, and prayed.

turns.speaker: Roger
turns.text:
Thank you for what You have given us.

Help me care for it well.

And show me where I can be useful today.
turns.instruction: A sincere private prayer. Let the specific meaning guide the emotion: fear, longing, gratitude or trust. Clearly voiced, not whispered or sermon-like.

turns.speaker: Narrator
turns.text: Then he stood up and went to work.
